Week 70 Appendix: The Fund That Would Not Yield

A settlement built a $1.776 billion executive fund and permanent tax immunity, testing whether resistance can catch harm before it hardens into law.

This week centered on the creation and immediate unraveling of a $1.776 billion DOJ 'Anti-Weaponization Fund,' established via a legally dubious settlement that dropped Trump's IRS lawsuit in exchange for permanent tax-audit immunity for Trump and his family, and a discretionary compensation pool potentially available to January 6 defendants. The fund triggered bipartisan Senate revolt, resignations (Treasury general counsel), lawsuits by Capitol Police officers, and House legislation to kill it—yet it proceeded regardless. Simultaneously, Trump continued a purge of Republican critics through primaries (Massie, Cassidy, Raffensperger), demanded the Senate parliamentarian's removal and filibuster elimination, and pursued self-glorifying projects (National Garden of American Heroes, triumphal arch, taxpayer-funded evangelical rally). Courts delivered mixed signals: some blocked ICE overreach and dismissed vindictive prosecutions, while SCOTUS continued gutting Voting Rights Act enforcement. Congress abdicated war-powers oversight on Iran by canceling votes it might have lost.
